leads.title: Obergefell v. Hodges, U.S. Supreme Court
leads.documents: Invalidated Louisiana same-sex marriage bans (1988/1999 Civil Code provisions and 2004 constitutional bans on marriage and civil unions); requires state to license same-sex marriages since June 26, 2015; Governor Bobby Jindal said state would comply two days later.
leads.detail: Citation visible: U.S. Supreme Court ruling June 26, 2015

leads.title: Bostock v. Clayton County, U.S. Supreme Court
leads.documents: Holds discrimination in employment on basis of sexual orientation or gender identity is discrimination on basis of sex under Title VII; provides employment protection in Louisiana where state law lacks comprehensive protections.
leads.detail: Citation visible: June 15, 2020, consolidated with Altitude Express, Inc. v. Zarda and R.G. & G.R. Harris Funeral Homes Inc. v. EEOC

leads.title: Robicheaux v. Caldwell - U.S. District Court decision
leads.documents: Federal challenge to Louisiana refusal to recognize same-sex marriages from other jurisdictions; Judge Martin Feldman ruled for state Sept 3, 2014 on biological-parents interest, then reversed for plaintiffs after Obergefell on remand from Fifth Circuit.
leads.detail: Citation visible: External links: U.S. District Court decision in Robicheaux v. Caldwell, September 3, 2014; appeal to Fifth Circuit Court of Appeals unresolved at time of Obergefell

leads.title: Costanza v. Caldwell - state court
leads.documents: State-court challenge to marriage ban; Judge Edward Rubin found prohibition on married same-sex couples adopting unconstitutional and granted first same-sex adoption Sept 22, 2014; appeal argued Jan 29, 2015 left unresolved by Obergefell.
leads.detail: Citation visible: Judge Edward Rubin ruling September 22, 2014

leads.title: Adar v. Smith / Pavan v. Smith
leads.documents: Documents birth-certificate machinery for same-sex parents: Louisiana successfully defended refusal to amend certificate for Louisiana-born child adopted in New York by married same-sex couple; Supreme Court rejected Lambda Legal review Oct 11, 2011; Obergefell and Pavan v. Smith (June 2017) require equal marriage-related rights including listing, though 2021 options only mother/father.
leads.detail: Citation visible: U.S. Supreme Court denial Oct 11, 2011, Lambda Legal representing plaintiffs; Pavan v. Smith June 2017

leads.title: Cook v. Sullivan, Louisiana Supreme Court (2021)
leads.documents: Parenting/custody precedent limiting unmarried same-sex second-parent rights; gave sole custody to biological mother ruling other woman not parent despite acting as second parent for years.
leads.detail: Citation visible: Louisiana Supreme Court decided 2021

leads.title: Louisiana hate crime statute (1997) and Matthew Shepard and James Byrd Jr. Hate Crimes Prevention Act
leads.documents: State penalty-enhancement law covers crimes motivated by victim sexual orientation or perceived sexual orientation, first in Deep South after 5-year lobbying; does not include gender identity, which must be prosecuted federally under 2009 federal Act signed by President Barack Obama.
leads.detail: Citation visible: Passed 1997; federal Act signed October 2009

leads.title: Louisiana Office of Motor Vehicles and Louisiana Vital Records gender-marker policy
leads.documents: Transgender rights machinery: allows change of gender marker on driver's license with physician statement confirming successful sex reassignment surgery; new birth certificate upon certified court order with proof of diagnosis as transsexual/pseudo-hermaphrodite and surgery changing anatomical structure.
leads.detail: Citation visible: Quoted Vital Records court-order standard in article text

leads.title: 2023 Louisiana ban on gender-affirming healthcare for minors / 2022 transgender sports ban
leads.documents: State Senate passed June 5, 2023 bill to ban puberty blockers, hormones, surgeries for minors effective Jan 1, 2024; Governor Edwards vetoed 3 bills June 2023, Legislature overrode in July 2023 to enact healthcare ban; 2021 sports bill passed House 77-17 Senate 29-6 vetoed as discrimination, veto override failed by 2 votes; June 2022 ban on transgender girls in public-school sports passed with veto-proof two-thirds so Gov. John Bel Edwards did not veto; insurance/Medicaid do not cover transition care.
leads.detail: Citation visible: Votes and dates as stated; signed/veto actions by Governor John Bel Edwards

leads.title: Public Religion Research Institute (PRRI) polls and Louisiana's Equality Profile - via Movement Advancement Project
leads.documents: Institutional tracking of legal status and climate: PRRI 2017 found 48% support same-sex marriage, 61% support anti-discrimination law; PRRI 2022 found 62% support same-sex marriage, 80% support anti-discrimination law covering sexual orientation/gender identity, 61% oppose religious refusal; MAP profile maps statewide equality gaps.
